definitions.english: Income is the money you receive from allowance, gifts, or small jobs.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso ke chelete eo o e fumanang ho tswa ho chelete ya pokotho, dimpho kapa mesebetsi e menyenyane.

definitions.english: When someone gives you money, that is income.
definitions.sesotho: Ha motho a o fa chelete, ke moputso.
Chelete ya pokotho ya hao ke moputso.

definitions.english: Income is money coming in. Expenses are money going out.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso ke chelete e kenang. Ditshenyehelo ke chelete e tswang.

definitions.english: If your parents give you M30 per week, that is weekly income.
definitions.sesotho: Haeba batswadi ba o fa M30 ka beke, ke moputso wa beke.

definitions.english: Income is money received regularly from work or other sources.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso ke chelete e fumanwang kgafetsa ho tswa mosebetsing kapa mehloding e meng.

definitions.english: Income is the flow of money into your possession.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso ke phallo ya chelete e kenang matsohong a hao.

definitions.english: Sources include wages, allowances, business profits, and investment returns.
definitions.sesotho: Mehlodi e kenyelletsa meputso, dipokotho, phaello ya kgwebo le matsete.

definitions.english: Gross income is before deductions. Net income is what you receive.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso o felletseng ke pele ho ditefello. Moputso o hlwekileng ke seo o se fumanang.

definitions.english: Regular income helps you plan and budget.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso o tloaelehileng o o thusa ho rera le ho etsa tekanyetso.

definitions.english: Income includes earned income, unearned income, and transfer payments.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso o kenyelletsa moputso o sebetswang, o sa sebetsweng le ditefello tsa phetiso.

definitions.english: Disposable income equals gross income minus taxes.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso o sebediswang o lekana le moputso o felletseng ho tlosa makgetho.

definitions.english: Income streams can be active or passive.
definitions.sesotho: Mehlodi ya moputso e ka ba e sebetsang kapa e sa sebetseng.

definitions.english: Income diversification is key to financial resilience.
definitions.sesotho: Ho fapanya mehlodi ya moputso ke senotlolo sa botsitso ba lichelete.

definitions.english: Student income includes bursaries, part-time work, and entrepreneurship.
definitions.sesotho: Moputso wa moithuti o kenyelletsa dibursary, mosebetsi wa nakwana le kgwebo.

examples.english: Your grandmother gives you M10. That is income!
examples.sesotho: Nkhono o o fa M10. Ke moputso!

examples.english: You help wash dishes and get M5. That is income.
examples.sesotho: O thusa ho hlatswa dijana mme o fumana M5. Ke moputso.

examples.english: Your parents give you M20 pocket money every week.
examples.sesotho: Batswadi ba o fa M20 ya pokotho beke le beke.

examples.english: You sell old toys and get M15.
examples.sesotho: O rekisa dipapadi tsa kgale mme o fumana M15.

examples.english: You receive M50 for your birthday. That is special income.
examples.sesotho: O fumana M50 ka letsatsi la hao la tswalo. Ke moputso o kgethehileng.

examples.english: Part-time job at M25/hour for 20 hours = M500 weekly.
examples.sesotho: Mosebetsi wa nakwana ka M25/ka hora dihora tse 20 = M500 ka beke.

examples.english: Sell 10 items at M15 each = M150 business income.
examples.sesotho: Rekisa dintho tse 10 ka M15 ka bonngwe = M150 moputso wa kgwebo.

examples.english: Monthly allowance of M300 is regular income.
examples.sesotho: Chelete ya kgwedi ya M300 ke moputso o tloaelehileng.
Fumana M200 ka ho thusa moahelani.

examples.english: Interest from savings = M20. That is investment income.
examples.sesotho: Phaello ho tswa polokong = M20. Ke moputso wa matsete.

examples.english: Bursary M2,500 plus part-time M1,000 = M3,500 monthly.
examples.sesotho: Bursary M2,500 le mosebetsi wa nakwana M1,000 = M3,500 ka kgwedi.

examples.english: Freelance: 5 projects at M400 = M2,000 monthly.
examples.sesotho: Freelance: diprojeke tse 5 ka M400 = M2,000 ka kgwedi.

examples.english: M50,000 invested at 6 percent = M3,000 annual interest.
examples.sesotho: M50,000 e kentsweng ka 6% = M3,000 phaello ka selemo.

examples.english: Tutoring: 10 students at M200 = M2,000 monthly.
examples.sesotho: Ho ruta: baithuti ba 10 ka M200 = M2,000 ka kgwedi.

examples.english: Mixed income streams create financial stability.
examples.sesotho: Mehlodi e fapaneng ya moputso e bopa botsitso ba lichelete.

misconceptions.english: Income is only from jobs — FALSE! Gifts count too.
misconceptions.sesotho: Moputso o tswa mesebetsing feela — HA SE NNETE! Dimpho le tsona di balwa.

misconceptions.english: More income means more problems — FALSE! More opportunities.
misconceptions.sesotho: Moputso o mongata o bolela mathata — HA SE NNETE! Menyetla e mengata.

misconceptions.english: Only adults have income — FALSE! Children can earn.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ke batho ba baholo feela ba nang le moputso — HA SE NNETE! Bana le bona ba ka fumana.

misconceptions.english: You need a full-time job for income — FALSE! Part-time counts.
misconceptions.sesotho: O hloka mosebetsi wa nako yohle — HA SE NNETE! Wa nakwana le wona o balwa.

misconceptions.english: Income is always money — FALSE! Goods can be income.
misconceptions.sesotho: Moputso ke chelete kamehla — HA SE NNETE! Thepa le yona e ka ba moputso.

misconceptions.english: All income should be spent — FALSE! Save a portion.
misconceptions.sesotho: Moputso wohle o lokela ho sebediswa — HA SE NNETE! Boloka karolo.

misconceptions.english: Bursary money needs no management — FALSE! It requires budgeting.
misconceptions.sesotho: Chelete ya bursary ha e hloke taolo — HA SE NNETE! E hloka tekanyetso.

misconceptions.english: Side income need not be reported — FALSE! Tax may apply.
misconceptions.sesotho: Moputso wa lehlakoreng ha o hloke ho tlalehwa — HA SE NNETE! Makgetho a ka sebetsa.

misconceptions.english: Passive income means no work — FALSE! Requires upfront effort.
misconceptions.sesotho: Moputso o sa sebetseng o bolela ho se sebetse — HA SE NNETE! O hloka boikitlaetso pele.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to learn how to earn more money?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho ithuta ho fumana chelete e ngata?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about budgeting your income?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue ka tekanyetso ya moputso?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to know how to save from income?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho tseba ho boloka ho tswa moputsong?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we explore student business ideas?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re hlahlobe mehopolo ya dikgwebo tsa baithuti?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to understand gross vs net income?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho utlwisisa phapang ya gross le net?

how_to.english: Help with chores to earn pocket money.
Ask grandparents for small jobs to earn money.
Sell old toys you no longer use.
Find part-time work in your community.
Offer tutoring services to younger students.
how_to.sesotho: Fana ka ho ruta baithuti ba banyane.

how_to.english: Sell items you make or no longer need.
how_to.sesotho: Rekisa dintho tseo o di etsang.

why.english: Income helps you buy things you need.
why.sesotho: Moputso o thusa ho reka ditlhoko.

why.english: Saving from income builds good habits.
why.sesotho: Ho boloka ho tswa moputsong ho haha ditlwaelo.
Mehlodi e mengata e bopa botsitso.

why.english: Passive income builds wealth over time.
why.sesotho: O sa sebetseng o haha maruo.
Boikemelo bo hloka taolo ya moputso.

situation.english: You earn M10 helping a neighbour. Should you spend it all or save some?
situation.sesotho: O fumana M10 ka ho thusa moahelani. O sebedise tsohle kapa o boloke tse ding?

advice.english: Save M3 and spend M7. Always save something from what you earn.
advice.sesotho: Boloka M3 mme o sebedise M7. Dula o boloka ho tswa ho seo o se fumanang.

lesson.english: Saving from income builds good habits.
lesson.sesotho: Ho boloka ho tswa moputsong ho haha ditlwaelo.

situation.english: You can tutor for M50/hour (5 hours/week) or work at a shop for M25/hour (10 hours/week). Which earns more?
situation.sesotho: O ka ruta ka M50/ka hora (dihora tse 5) kapa lebenkeleng ka M25/ka hora (dihora tse 10). Ke efe e fumanang ho feta?

advice.english: Tutoring: M250/week. Shop: M250/week. Same! But tutoring uses less time.
advice.sesotho: Ho ruta: M250/ka beke. Lebenkele: M250/ka beke. Hoa tshwana! Empa ho ruta ho sebedisa nako e nyane.

lesson.english: Higher hourly rate means more free time.
lesson.sesotho: Phaello e phahameng ka hora e bolela nako e ngata ya phomolo.

situation.english: You have two income options: Fixed job M2,000/month or freelance averaging M2,500/month but irregular. Which is safer?
situation.sesotho: O na le dikgetho tse pedi: Mosebetsi o tsitsitseng M2,000/kgwedi kapa freelance M2,500/kgwedi empa e sa tshwarahala. E feng e bolokehileng?

advice.english: Fixed job is more stable for budgeting. Freelance offers more but riskier.
advice.sesotho: Mosebetsi o tsitsitseng o bolokehile bakeng sa tekanyetso. Freelance e fana ka ho feta empa e kotsi.

lesson.sesotho: Moputso o tsitsitseng o etsa tekanyetso e be bonolo.
